title: The Crucifixion and Death of Jesus

questions.question: Pilate took Jesus and flogged Him. The soldiers plaited a crown of what and put it on His head, and arrayed Him in a purple robe?
questions.explanation: John 19:2 (ESV): "And the soldiers twisted together a crown of thorns and put it on his head and arrayed him in a purple robe."

questions.question: What did the soldiers mockingly say as they struck Jesus with their hands?
options: "Show us a sign, son of God!"
questions.explanation: John 19:3 (ESV): "They came up to him, saying, 'Hail, King of the Jews!' and struck him with their hands."

questions.question: Pilate brought Jesus out wearing the crown and purple robe and said to the Jews, "Behold the man!" What did the chief priests and officers cry?
questions.explanation: John 19:6 (ESV): "When the chief priests and the officers saw him, they cried out, 'Crucify him, crucify him!'"

questions.question: When Pilate said he found no guilt in Jesus, the Jews said Jesus ought to die because He had claimed to be what?
questions.explanation: John 19:7 (ESV): "The Jews answered him, 'We have a law, and according to that law he ought to die because he has made himself the Son of God.'"

questions.question: When the Jews threatened Pilate saying "If you release this man, you are not Caesar's friend," what did Pilate do?
options: He brought Jesus out and sat down on the judgment seat at the place called The Stone Pavement
He immediately ordered the release of Barabbas
He washed his hands before the multitude
He wrote a letter of defense to Caesar
questions.correctAnswer: He brought Jesus out and sat down on the judgment seat at the place called The Stone Pavement
questions.explanation: John 19:13 (ESV): "So when Pilate heard these words, he brought Jesus out and sat down on the judgment seat at a place called The Stone Pavement..."

questions.question: What was the inscription that Pilate wrote and had placed on the cross?
options: "Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews"
questions.correctAnswer: "Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews"
questions.explanation: John 19:19 (ESV): "Pilate also wrote an inscription and put it on the cross. It read, 'Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews.'"

questions.question: In what three languages was the inscription on the cross written?
questions.explanation: John 19:20 (ESV): "...and it was written in Aramaic, in Latin, and in Greek."

questions.question: Standing by the cross of Jesus were several women. To which disciple did Jesus entrust the care of His mother?
questions.explanation: John 19:26-27 (ESV): "When Jesus therefore saw his mother and the disciple whom he loved standing nearby, he said to his mother, 'Woman, behold, your son!' Then he said to the disciple, 'Behold, your mother!'"

questions.question: After this, Jesus, knowing all was finished, said "I thirst." A jar of sour wine was there. How was it given to Him?
options: They put a sponge full of sour wine on a hyssop branch and held it to his mouth
They handed him a cup directly with care
They poured it on his head to mock him greatly
They tilted a full jar to his lips carefully
questions.correctAnswer: They put a sponge full of sour wine on a hyssop branch and held it to his mouth
questions.explanation: John 19:29 (ESV): "A jar full of sour wine stood there, so they put a sponge full of the sour wine on a hyssop branch and held it to his mouth."

questions.question: After receiving the sour wine, what were Jesus' final words before He bowed His head and gave up His spirit?
options: "Father, into your hands I commit my spirit."
"My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?"
questions.explanation: John 19:30 (ESV): "When Jesus had received the sour wine, he said, 'It is finished,' and he bowed his head and gave up his spirit."

questions.question: The soldiers decided not to divide Jesus' tunic since it was seamless, woven in one piece. Scripture was thus fulfilled saying "They divided my garments among them, and for my clothing they cast lots." This is from which Psalm?
questions.explanation: John 19:24 (ESV) cites this fulfillment. The source is Psalm 22:18: "they divide my garments among them, and for my clothing they cast lots."

questions.question: To ensure the bodies would not remain on the cross on the Sabbath, the Jews asked that legs be broken. When the soldiers came to Jesus, why did they not break His legs?
options: They saw that he was already dead
The Scripture commanded it be so
questions.correctAnswer: They saw that he was already dead
questions.explanation: John 19:33 (ESV): "But when they came to Jesus and saw that he was already dead, they did not break his legs."

questions.question: Instead of breaking Jesus' legs, what did a soldier do?
options: Pierced his side with a spear, and at once blood and water came out
Laid a seal on the tomb securely
Tore his seamless tunic into four parts
Cast lots for his remaining sandals
questions.correctAnswer: Pierced his side with a spear, and at once blood and water came out
questions.explanation: John 19:34 (ESV): "But one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and at once there came out blood and water."

questions.question: Who was Joseph of Arimathea who cared for the body of Jesus?
options: A disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews
A Roman official sympathetic to Jesus
A Pharisee who had argued for Jesus in the council
A Galilean merchant who had financed Jesus' ministry
questions.correctAnswer: A disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews
questions.explanation: John 19:38 (ESV): "After these things Joseph of Arimathea, who was a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews, asked Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus."

questions.question: Who came with Joseph of Arimathea to help bury Jesus, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes?
questions.explanation: John 19:39 (ESV): "Nicodemus also, who earlier had come to Jesus by night, came bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about seventy-five pounds in weight."

key_verse_text: When Jesus had received the sour wine, he said, "It is finished," and he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.
